book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook entry starts with the institution: MUDRA set up in 2015 under PMMY to refinance lenders for loans up to 10 lakh in three bands, then lists who is eligible. Here, after a one-line hook on Mudra Bank, the video drops to first principles: what an enterprise is, its four sizes, why micro and small ones matter (jobs), and the credit gap that holds them back; only then the scheme arrives as the government's answer, with eligibility and examples, then the lending chain (partner lenders, three bands, risk-based rate), and last the refinance function that gives Mudra its name, worked through one trader's loan. The why-before-what order gives the scheme a reason, but the institution named in the title waits more than three minutes.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Zoom from the widest category to one transaction: enterprise, its sizes, the group that matters, its problem, the scheme, who qualifies, who lends what at what price, and finally one loan's refinance in numbers.

talmel_summary: The picture usually runs ahead of the voice, often by 1-2 s and sometimes by 5-10 s (the 11 crore jobs box, the '>' sign, the 1 lakh and 10% labels, the loan bands), so the learner reads before hearing. Where it works, the picture does the step: the eligibility tag drops onto the group it filters, ten loan arrows rain from the bank onto entrepreneurs and then shrink to one, and the loan paper travels back to Mudra while money arcs to the bank. Weak: the credit problem and the 1.25 crore figure are spoken with no picture, the 'Registered' arrow points the wrong way, the refinance sum is never written, and a 17 s transcript gap (274.9-291.6 s) hides the 'low / flexible' and 'refinance' lead-in.

voice.notes: About 170 words per minute, calm and even, a lecture tone. Amounts are read the Indian way (50 hazaar, 5 lakh, 1 lakh 5 hazaar), which the transcript turns into 5,000,000 and 10,000,000. Unpacking with 'yaani', framing with 'maan ke chalte hain' and 'actually ye scheme kuch is tarah work karti hai'. One second-person stretch ('agar aap repair shop chalate hain') makes eligibility personal. No pauses before the lists, so the three lists run together.

game_ideas.player_does: Runs a partner bank's Mudra desk for a day: registers with Mudra, then serves a queue (tea stall wanting 40,000, tailor wanting 3 lakh, workshop wanting 8 lakh, a registered company, a dairy farm), choosing Shishu, Kishor, Tarun or 'not eligible', and setting the rate from a risk card.
game_ideas.process_happens: The loan arrow fills the right segment of the range bar and the money goes to the applicant; the bank's cash meter drops with each loan; when it runs low the player can send loan papers to Mudra and money arcs back.
game_ideas.win: Every eligible applicant served at a rate matching their risk, with refinance used before cash runs out.
game_ideas.lose: A Mudra loan to the registered company or the farm is bounced back by Mudra; an amount in the wrong band flashes the band's limit; letting cash hit zero sends the remaining applicants to a moneylender at a much higher rate.
game_ideas.concept: Mudra Bank and partner financial institutions

game_ideas.player_does: Sorts enterprise cards (repair shop, private limited company, poultry or dairy unit, artisan, food cart, large factory) into 'PMMY covered' and 'not covered', then places the covered ones on the Shishu / Kishor / Tarun bar by the loan they need.
game_ideas.process_happens: A correct card lands under the teal 'non-corporate & non-farm' tag and its loan arrow drops into the matching band.
game_ideas.win: All cards in the right group and band.
game_ideas.lose: A company card dropped in 'covered' gets stamped 'registered company', a farm card 'farm activity', with the rule shown; an amount placed past a band's edge is pushed to the next band.
game_ideas.concept: PMMY (2015) and its beneficiaries: non-corporate, non-farm MSEs

game_ideas.player_does: Has 3 lakh to lend at 10% to traders who each want 1 lakh; after three loans the cash is gone; the player decides whether to refinance with Mudra at a 5% charge.
game_ideas.process_happens: Refinancing returns cash for the next traders while the bank keeps the gap between the 10% it earns and the 5% it pays; not refinancing leaves the queue waiting.
game_ideas.win: Serve all six traders and end with a positive interest margin.
game_ideas.lose: Refusing refinance strands three traders; refinancing at a charge above 10% shows the bank losing money on every loan (the game follows a standard refinance model, not the video's 1.05 lakh figure, which needs checking).
game_ideas.concept: benefit of refinance: funds to lend again

checks_learned: Normalise Indian number words (lakh, crore) before comparing transcript numbers with on-screen numbers: '5 lakh' came out as 5,000,000.
A figure the voice compares against (1.25 crore) must be on screen next to the figure it is compared with (11 crore).
An arrow must point from the actor to the target the narration names: banks register with Mudra, so the 'Registered' arrow points to Mudra.
When the voice says 'the calculation can be seen here', every step of the sum must be on screen (1 lakh + 10K - 5K = 1.05 lakh).
A problem sentence in the script (no loans, moneylenders, cannot grow) must get its own picture before the solution appears.
Institution names and status should go to a fact check (MUDRA is usually described as a SIDBI subsidiary, not a bank; the interest rule may be outdated).
No real logos, emblems or photos of real people; replace with generic drawings.
A transcript word whose end time lies more than 5 s after its start hides a gap (274.9-291.6 s here); flag it.
Numbers should not appear more than about 2 s before they are spoken (here up to 10 s early).

teaching_best.why: Before the scheme, a real figure (11 crore jobs) and a contrast (large firms far fewer) make the learner care why micro and small enterprises need help.
'Non-corporate, non-farm' is unpacked twice in plain words and then made personal with 'agar aap repair shop chalate hain'.
The bank's limited money is voiced as the problem first, so refinance arrives as the way out, not as a definition.
One trader's 1 lakh loan carries the refinance idea with every amount on the picture.

teaching_weak.why: The credit problem (moneylenders, no growth) is told, not shown, and then left behind.
Three lists (4 sizes, 6 lender types, 3 loan bands) come within about 3 minutes with no check or recap.
The 'base rate + 0-7%' rule is stated as fact; it should be checked against current rules.
The refinance arithmetic is not written out and refinance is described like selling the loan; doubtful as a model.
No recap of the chain (Mudra, partner lender, borrower) at the end.
